The Soviet Union. A communist state established in nineteen twenty-two after the Russian Revolution, comprising a federation of Soviet socialist republics led by the Communist Party and spanning the vast territory of the former Russian Empire. Founded by Vladimir Lenin and built into a totalitarian superpower by Joseph Stalin, the USSR industrialized at breakneck speed, conducted massive social engineering through collectivization and purges, and emerged from World War II as one of the world's two superpowers. The regime pursued revolutionary communist ideology while maintaining absolute party control, creating a planned economy and one-party state that served as the model for communist regimes worldwide. The Soviet Union collapsed in nineteen ninety-one after decades of economic stagnation, internal contradictions, and failed reform, reshaping the post-Cold War world.

The Russian Revolution began with the February Revolution in nineteen seventeen, overthrowing Tsar Nicholas II. The Bolshevik seizure of power in October nineteen seventeen under Lenin concluded the revolutionary turmoil. Lenin's Bolsheviks won the Russian Civil War from nineteen eighteen to nineteen twenty-two against the White anti-communist forces, establishing a dictatorship of the proletariat supposedly representing workers' interests. The Union of Soviet Socialist Republics was formally created in nineteen twenty-two, uniting Russia, Ukraine, Byelorussia, and the Caucasian republics under a centralized communist party hierarchy.

Lenin introduced the New Economic Policy from nineteen twenty-one to nineteen twenty-eight, a pragmatic retreat from war communism that allowed limited market mechanisms while maintaining party control. The regime imposed atheism as state doctrine, persecuting the Russian Orthodox Church and other religions. Lenin's death in nineteen twenty-four sparked a succession struggle. Joseph Stalin eventually defeated rivals, consolidating power by the late nineteen twenties.

Stalin pursued Five-Year Plans beginning in nineteen twenty-eight to rapidly industrialize and build military power through centralized state planning. Collectivization of agriculture from nineteen twenty-eight to nineteen thirty-three forcibly consolidated peasant farms, causing widespread famine. The Ukrainian Famine, called the Holodomor, killed millions. Stalin's Purges from nineteen thirty-six to nineteen thirty-eight eliminated perceived enemies, executing generals, party officials, and intellectuals on fabricated charges, creating a climate of terror and paranoia.

Nazi Germany invaded the USSR in nineteen forty-one in Operation Barbarossa, forcing an alliance with Britain and the United States against the Axis powers. Soviet forces bore the brunt of the Nazi war effort, suffering over twenty-five million casualties but ultimately defeating Germany in a brutal campaign pushing Soviet armies to Berlin. The USSR emerged as a superpower, having liberated Eastern Europe and establishing communist satellite states under Soviet control.

The Cold War from nineteen forty-five to nineteen ninety-one was a global conflict between Soviet communism and American capitalism. The USSR built a vast military apparatus, including nuclear weapons first tested in nineteen forty-nine, developing intercontinental missile capability that created the threat of mutually assured destruction. Soviet-backed communism spread to Eastern Europe, China, Vietnam, Cuba, and elsewhere. By the nineteen seventies and nineteen eighties, the Soviet economy was inefficient and stagnant. Mikhail Gorbachev attempted reform through Glasnost, meaning openness, and Perestroika, meaning restructuring, but these unleashed forces he could not control. The USSR dissolved in nineteen ninety-one after failed hardline coup attempts and the independence of constituent republics, ending the Cold War and reshaping the global balance of power.
